title: Things you can and can’t count
intro: Some nouns can be counted: one chair, two chairs. Others can’t: you can’t say “two waters” or “an advice”. Uncountable nouns have no plural and never take “a” or “an”. Many of the most common Indian-English mistakes come from these words.

rules.rule: Countable nouns have a plural and can take a/an.
Uncountable nouns have no plural and no a/an. Use “some”, “a lot of”, or “a piece of”.
examples: Can I give you some advice?
She gave me a useful piece of information.

rules.rule: These are always uncountable: advice, information, furniture, luggage, baggage, equipment, news, homework, work, research, feedback, knowledge, traffic, weather.
examples: We got a lot of feedback.

mistakes.right: He gave me a lot of advice.

mistakes.why: “Information” is uncountable, so no “an” and no plural.
“News” ends in -s but it is singular.

ex.q: I have a lot of ___ to finish tonight.
She has three ___ for the project.
Thank you for all the informations.
ex.fixed: Thank you for all the information.

ex.q: We need to buy some new equipments.
ex.fixed: We need to buy some new equipment.

ex.q: There were too many traffics this morning.
ex.fixed: There were too much traffic this morning.

ex.q: Let me give you a piece of ___: sleep early.
Correct this: “My teacher gave me many good advices.”
a: My teacher gave me a lot of good advice
My teacher gave me lots of good advice
My teacher gave me some good advice
My teacher gave me much good advice
ex.y: “Advice” has no plural: a lot of good advice.

talk: Talk about the best advice someone gave you and the news you heard this week. Be careful with “advice”, “news” and “information”.
